newsitem.title: USA: NASD names former OCC official to oversee munis.
newsitem.headline: NASD names former OCC official to oversee munis.

text.p: NASD Regulation Inc said Friday it appointed Malcolm Northam, a former deputy director of the U.S. Office of the Comptroller of the Currency, as the group's first director of municipal industry compliance.

"Compliance in the municipal securities sector is one of NASD Regulation's top priorities and Mac will help us maintain and improve a vigorous and uniform national policy," Elisse Walter, NASD Regulation's CEO, said in announcing the appointment.

"In this new position, Northam will be NASD Regulation's primary liaison on municipal securities matters with Municipal Securities Rulemaking Board, Securities and Exchange Commission and an array of industry and investor groups," NASD said.

While Northam will be named director of "fixed income" securities when he joins NASD on May 5, he will be "clearly focused on the regulation of all aspects of municipal securities activities by broker/dealer firms," Walter said.

Northam was with OCC from 1969 to 1990 as a bank examiner and as deputy director of the division. He spent the last two years handling compliance issues for The Secura Group in Falls Church, Va., NASD said. From 1990 to 1995 Northam was founding partner of Alexandria, Va.-based Securities Risk Management, where he developed nationwide training programs for banks and securities firms, NASD said.
NASD said Northam will educate broker-dealers on municipal, government and derivative securities matters and he will work with NASD Regulation's 14 district offices on the issues.
